[[Hyattsville, Maryland|Hyattsville]], [[Maryland]] | former_school(s)= | awards = Big East Player of the Year 2007 }} {{otherpeople2|Jeff Green}} '''Jeffrey Lynn Green''' (born [[August 28]], [[1986]]) is a collegiate men's [[basketball]] player in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]]. He attends [[Georgetown University]] where he is currently in his junior year.{{cite web |url= http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=22425 |title= ESPN Statistics |work= [[ESPN]].com |date= 2007 |accessdate= 2007-03-19}} ==Background== Jeff Green was born in in [[Cheverly, Maryland|Cheverly]], [[Maryland]] to Jeffrey Green Sr. and Felicia Akingube. He attended [[Northwestern High School (Hyattsville, Maryland)|Northwestern High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland|Hyattsville]], [[Maryland]], where he led the NHS Wildcats to the state basketball championship in 2004. Green was successfully recruited by [[Georgetown University]] coach [[Craig Esherick]] in 2003. However, Esherick was fired before Green arrived on campus (Esherick's last season as coach went 13-15). [[John Thompson III]] was hired as the new coach. Ironically, the two key recruits of Esherick's tenure, Green and center [[Roy Hibbert]], would be the key components of Thompson's future success.{{cite news |url= http://www.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20061116&content_id=1415039&oid=2&vkey=29 |title= Rivalry revived |first= Brendon |last= Desrochers |work= [http://www.sny.tv SNY.tv] |date= [[2006-11-16]] |accessdate= 2007-03-19}} ==Key attributes== At 6'10" and 235 pounds, Green plays forward under Coach [[John Thompson III]]. He is the captain of the squad. Thompson has stated in a [[Sports Illustrated]] interview: "You'll stop and think when I say this, but it's true: Jeff Green is the smartest player I've ever coached. You would know this better than most: that's a hell of a statement."{{cite news |url= http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/writers/grant_wahl/11/15/cbb.mailbag/1.html |title= The 'Bag is back |first= Grant |last= Wahl |work= [[ESPN]].com |date= [[2006-11-15]] |accessdate= 2007-03-19}} Green has evidently mastered the [[Princeton offense]], which Thompson learned and implemented during his tenure as player, assistant coach and then head coach of the [[Princeton University]] basketball team. Green was perhaps the key player in then-unranked Georgetown's monumental upset victory over top-ranked and undefeated [[Duke University]] in [[2006]].{{cite web |url= http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/03/02/AR2007030201921_2.html |title= Georgetown's Green: 'New-Age Scottie Pippen' |first= Camille |last= Powell |work= [[The Washington Post]] |date= [[2007-03-03]] |accessdate= 2007-03-19}} Numerous quotes from teammates have attested to Green's calm yet disciplined demeanor, and his ability to focus not only himself but the other players on his team. Despite his unselfish style, Green has established himself as a player who can be counted on to hit important shots at the end of close games. During the 2006-2007 season, Green hit three game-winning shots in the final seconds of games. The most notable of these was his game-winning shot against Vanderbilt in the Sweet 16 round of the NCAA Tournament. With the Hoyas down one, Green squeezed past a double-team and hit a difficult shot with 2.5 seconds left in the game. Some observers claimed that Green traveled on the play, but the officials stated that Green's move was legal. Green's greatest strengths as a player are his intellect and versatility--he is equally effective in defense and offense, and is good under pressure. This has made him an ideal asset for Coach Thompson's [[Princeton offense]], a complicated strategy involving movement and flexibility. Green's weaknesses are streaky shooting, and that he can sometimes be unselfish to a fault.{{cite web |url= http://insider.espn.go.com/nbadraft/draft/tracker/player?playerId=18886&draftyear=2007 |title= Jeff Green |work= [http://www.espn.com espn.com] |date= 2007 |accessdate= 2007-06-18}} ==Honors== Jeff Green won the [[2005]] [[Big East]] Rookie of the Year award along with [[Rudy Gay]] of the [[University of Connecticut]]. In addition, Green was named to the All-Big East Second Team in [[2006]] along with teammate [[Roy Hibbert]].{{ref|bigeast}} In [[2007]], Green and teammate Roy Hibbert were unanimous selections to the All-Big East First Team. After his 30-point performance in the [[2007]] [[Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|Big East Tournament]] Semi-final against [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]] and his 21-point performance in the Championship against the [[University of Pittsburgh]], Green was also named Most Outstanding Player of the [[2007]] [[Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|Big East Tournament]] as the [[Hoyas]] went on to claim their first [[Big East]] title since [[1989]]. ==Future== Jeff Green is a probable [[NBA Draft Lottery|NBA lottery]] pick.{{cite news |url= http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/02/24/AR2007022401393.html |title= The Grass Gets Greener |first= Mike |last= Wise |work= [[The Washington Post]] |date= [[2007-02-27]] |accessdate= 2007-03-19}} On June 18 (the deadline for withdrawl), after several weeks of uncertainty, Green announced that he will remain in the [[2007 NBA Draft]]. He is currently expected to fall somewhere between lottery pick numbers five and twelve. His teammate, Roy Hibbert, announced he will return to school for his senior year. Only four players in Georgetown history, now including Green, have left early for the [[NBA]].{{cite web |url= http://www.hoyasaxa.com/sports/archives/archive0603.htm#42 |title= Sweetney Chooses NBA Draft |work= [http://www.hoyasaxa.com HoyaSaxa.com] |date= [[2003-06-19]] |accessdate= 2007-03-19}} Green's official NBA measurements are 6'7.75" and 228 lbs. ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:1986 births|Green, Jeff]] [[Category:American basketball players|Green, Jeff]] [[Category:Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball players|Green, Jeff]] [[Category:Living people|Green, Jeff]] [[Category:People from Maryland|Green, Jeff]]
